ev.byz_fc_anadochos.archon.ok: Your noble sponsor held you over the font in a silken cloak and renounced Satan on your behalf. Your parents spent the evening receiving congratulations — and counting the cost.
ev.byz_fc_anadochos.neighbor.ok: The neighbour's eyes filled with tears when you were handed to him at the font. Since then your two houses have been one family: together at feasts, and together in trouble.
ev.byz_fc_anadochos.uncle: An uncle — keep it in the family
ev.byz_fc_anadochos.uncle.ok: Your uncle carried you round the font, swelling with pride. Family is family — and now spiritual family too.
ev.byz_fc_anadochos.title: The sponsor at the font
ev.byz_fc_anadochos.text: The fortieth day is near, and it is time to decide who will carry you to the font. The sponsor — the anadochos — will become your spiritual father and make your two families kin for life. Your father is thinking of asking someone grander and richer than you: a great honour, but it calls for generous gifts. Or you could ask an old friend from next door, or one of your uncles.
ev.byz_fc_anadochos.note: At baptism the sponsor (anadochos) renounced Satan on the infant's behalf and answered for its upbringing in the faith. Baptism created spiritual kinship: the Council in Trullo (692) forbade a sponsor to marry the child's mother, and the eighth-century Ecloga extended the ban to the sponsor's son. A noble godfather was a real patron for a family.
ev.byz_fc_anadochos_letter.title: A word from the sponsor
ev.byz_fc_anadochos_letter.text: The noble sponsor who held you over the font has not forgotten his godchild. He summoned you, asked about your affairs, and you left with a purse of silver and a letter under his seal: "Assist the bearer." With such a letter many doors open by themselves.
ev.byz_fc_anadochos_kin.title: Spiritual kin
ev.byz_fc_anadochos_kin.text: For a long time you have had your eye on the {g:daughter|son} of the neighbour who was your sponsor at the font. But the priest only spread his hands: you are spiritual kin, and the Church will never bless such a marriage. You can't command the heart — and still less the law.
ev.byz_fc_eulogia.oil.ok: The neighbour anointed your brow and chest crosswise herself, whispering a prayer to the saint. By morning the cough had eased, and your mother lit a candle to him.
ev.byz_fc_eulogia.icon.ok: The painter set the saint at full length on a cypress panel, with a golden halo. The icon was hung above the cradle, and your mother, they say, stopped weeping at night at once.
ev.byz_fc_eulogia.wait.ok: "All children cough," your father decided. You coughed until spring, but you pulled through.
ev.byz_fc_eulogia.title: Oil from the saint's tomb
ev.byz_fc_eulogia.text: You have been coughing for three nights, and your mother never leaves the cradle. A neighbour back from a pilgrimage offers a little lead flask of oil from the lamp over a saint's tomb: anoint the baby's chest and it will pass. Your father wants instead to order a small icon of the saint from a painter, to hang above the cradle and guard you all your life — costly, but it will last for ages.
ev.byz_fc_eulogia.note: The Byzantines believed in the power of "blessings", eulogiai: pilgrims brought home oil from the lamps at saints' tombs, holy water and earth in little lead flasks. At Thessalonica fragrant myrrh was gathered from the tomb of Saint Demetrios. Icons hung in almost every house, and in the houses of the rich, in every room.
ev.byz_fc_eulogia_fair.title: The saint's fair
ev.byz_fc_eulogia_fair.text: For the feast of the saint whose oil anointed you as a baby, the whole family went to the panegyris — the fair at his church. You had never seen so many people: merchants from distant cities, jugglers, stalls of honey and spices, and in the church a queue to the tomb stretching to the gates.
ev.byz_fc_eulogia_icon.title: The icon over the cradle
ev.byz_fc_eulogia_icon.text: One night, when your heart was especially heavy, you lit the little lamp before the very icon that once hung over your cradle. The saint looked at you as sternly and kindly as in your childhood. Towards morning you rose from your knees knowing what to do.
